summary: Evaluate tree-sitter as the W2 AST substrate vs bespoke rowan-style, per ADR-0510 + Rust-purity doctrine

research.summary: Tree-sitter is a parser generator plus an incremental-parsing runtime: grammars are authored in a JavaScript DSL (grammar.js), `tree-sitter generate` emits a dependency-free C parser (LR(1) tables driven by a GLR runtime, optionally paired with a hand-written C external scanner), and the pure-C11 core library (~533 KB of source, 37 files, MIT, v0.26.9 as of 2026-05-19) re-parses after edits in time proportional to the edit by reusing unchanged subtrees from the old tree. Error recovery is cost-based GLR recovery that yields queryable ERROR and MISSING nodes, so in-progress agent code still produces usable trees. The S-expression query language (captures, fields, quantifiers, predicates) is proven at hyperscale for lint-style pattern gates but does no rewriting and its predicates execute host-side. The decisive gap for Oyatie is node identity: TSNode identity is a process-local subtree pointer plus byte positions — stable only when a subtree happens to be reused, never content-addressed — which is exactly the crux ADR-0517 (one-way door) already cited when it rejected tree-sitter as the substrate and ruled the destination is a bespoke safe-Rust, rowan-style, content-addressed AST ("tree-sitter-our-way"). Net: tree-sitter is a strong R1/R3/R4/R6 transitional adapter behind the WorkAreaTree trait (ADR-0510/0520) with an exception-ledger row for its C core, but it cannot be the destination, and markdown (R5) is explicitly weak in its ecosystem.
facts: CORE MODEL: 'Tree-sitter is a parser generator tool and an incremental parsing library'; design goals quoted as general 'enough to parse any programming language', fast 'enough to parse on every keystroke in a text editor', robust 'enough to provide useful results even in the presence of syntax errors', and dependency-free 'so that the runtime library (which is written in pure C11) can be embedded in any application' (tree-sitter.github.io index; github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter README). MIT license; latest release v0.26.9, 2026-05-19 (GitHub API, verified via gh).

ALGORITHM: 'Tree-sitter uses a GLR parser, a type of LR parser' (Wikipedia, consistent with docs). Generation resolves what it can statically — prec() 'resolves LR(1) Conflicts at parser-generation time', while prec.dynamic applies at runtime (grammar DSL docs). Runtime GLR machinery verified in lib/src/parser.c: StackVersion forking, ts_stack_merge() when paths reconverge, MAX_VERSION_COUNT = 6, ts_parser__condense_stack() which 'prunes any versions that have been marked for removal' and removes versions 'clearly worse than another version'; ambiguity resolution in ts_parser__select_tree() orders by error cost then ts_subtree_dynamic_precedence.

INCREMENTAL O(edit) MECHANISM: edit flow is two-step — 'First, you must edit the syntax tree, which adjusts the ranges of its nodes so that they stay in sync with the code' (TSInputEdit carries start/old_end/new_end in both bytes and row/col points), then ts_parser_parse is called with the old tree and the new tree shares structure (docs Advanced Parsing). Reuse conditions verified in parser.c: reusable_node tracking plus ts_parser__can_reuse_first_leaf — 'If the token was created in a state with the same set of lookaheads, it is reusable'; subtrees with ts_subtree_has_changes or ts_subtree_is_fragile are not reused; included-range differences invalidate reuse. ts_tree_get_changed_ranges 'indicate[s] areas where the hierarchical structure of syntax nodes (from root to leaf) has changed between the old and new trees' (api.h). Design influence explicitly credited to Wagner/Graham-era work: 'Practical Algorithms for Incremental Software Development Environments' (1997, CSD-97-946), 'Efficient and Flexible Incremental Parsing', 'Incremental Analysis of Real Programming Languages' (Tim Wagner, Berkeley Harmonia), 'Context Aware Scanning for Parsing Extensible Languages' (Van Wyk), and two LR error-recovery papers (docs index, Underlying Research).

ERROR RECOVERY: implemented in ts_parser__recover() in lib/src/parser.c — 'When the parser is in the error state, there are two strategies for recovering with a given lookahead token: 1. Find a previous state on the stack in which that lookahead token would be valid...' (the other being skipping tokens), governed by a cost model (ERROR_COST_PER_SKIPPED_TREE / _CHAR / _LINE) with ts_stack_record_summary and ts_parser__recover_to_state. Results surface as queryable nodes: (ERROR) for unrecognized text and (MISSING name) for 'zero-width inserted tokens' (query syntax docs). Recovery internals are code-level heuristics, not a documented stable contract.

GENERATED-PARSER MODEL: 'Tree-sitter grammars are written in JavaScript, and Tree-sitter uses a JavaScript runtime (the default being Node.js) to interpret JavaScript files' — JS needed only at generate time; 'tree-sitter generate' emits 'the C code required to parse this trivial language' (creating-parsers docs), compiled with any C compiler. Grammar DSL: seq/choice/repeat/optional, prec/prec.left/prec.right/prec.dynamic, conflicts array of 'intended' LR(1) conflicts, externals, word, supertypes, field() (DSL docs). External scanners: 'a set of C functions that you, the grammar author, can write by hand' in src/scanner.c for tokens regexes cannot express ('Indent and dedent tokens in Python', 'Heredocs in Bash and Ruby'); five functions create/destroy/serialize/deserialize/scan; serialized scanner state 'will ultimately be stored in the syntax tree so that the scanner can be restored to the right state when handling edits or ambiguities' (external-scanners docs).

RUNTIME CORE: pure C11, zero runtime deps; lib/src measured at 37 files, 532,546 bytes of source on master (GitHub API, 2026-06-09). Repo language split: Rust 64.3% (CLI/generator are Rust), C 24.2%, TypeScript 6.5% (GitHub). ABI: '#define TREE_SITTER_LANGUAGE_VERSION 15' / 'TREE_SITTER_MIN_COMPATIBLE_LANGUAGE_VERSION 13'; 'generally backwards-compatible with languages generated using older CLI versions, but is not forwards-compatible' (api.h). Grammars can also compile to WASM and load via ts_wasm_store_load_language / ts_parser_set_wasm_store (api.h). Parsing supports a progress callback for cancellation and 'will resume where it left off on the next call to ts_parser_parse' (api.h).

QUERY LANGUAGE: 'A query consists of one or more patterns, where each pattern is an S-expression that matches a certain set of nodes in a syntax tree'; @name captures; field-name child constraints (left:, object:); negated fields '(class_declaration !type_parameters)'; anonymous nodes in double quotes; wildcards (_) and _; supertype/subtype patterns; (ERROR) and (MISSING x) matchable (query syntax docs). Predicates #eq?/#not-eq?/#any-eq?, #match? (regex), #any-of?, #is?, and the #set! metadata directive exist, BUT: 'Predicates and directives are not handled directly by the Tree-sitter C library. They are just exposed in a structured form so that higher-level code can perform the filtering' (predicates docs). Queries are read-only matchers — no rewrite/transform facility in the engine (auto-fix layers like ast-grep are built on top); query results are not incrementally maintained across edits (upstream Discussion #1976 'Incremental queries'; re-running over ts_tree_get_changed_ranges is the supported pattern).

NODE IDENTITY (R2 crux): TSNode is 'typedef struct TSNode { uint32_t context[4]; const void *id; const TSTree *tree; } TSNode;' (api.h) — id is an internal subtree pointer, undocumented in the header beyond ts_node_eq 'Check if two nodes are identical.' Maintainer guidance (upstream Discussion #800, via search): node ids are 'a reliable (but sometimes conservative) way to detect that a sub tree hasn't changed. If a node is reused, its id is stable' — but nodes in the new tree otherwise get different ids, ids are process-local pointers (not stable across parses, processes, or machines), and there is no content hash anywhere in the model; identity is otherwise byte-range/positional. Official recommendation is to re-fetch nodes after edits; ts_node_edit exists only for keeping pre-edit TSNode instances usable ('This function is only rarely needed', api.h).

PERFORMANCE: the project publishes design targets ('every keystroke'), not an official benchmark table. Credible third-party measurements: Scala 3 corpus — 5,835-line Types.scala parsed in 73 ms vs Dotty parser 1,980 ms (27x), ~91 sloc/ms vs ~20 sloc/ms, and incrementally 'increase in 5474 lines results in only additional 60ms, as opposed to 244ms in Dotty' (eed3si9n.com); symflower reported 'a speedup by a factor of 36x' migrating JavaParser to tree-sitter (search-snippet level); performance is grammar-dependent — tree-sitter-haskell required a community fix titled 'Speeding up tree-sitter-haskell 50x' (owen.cafe, title-level; page returned 403). Max Brunsfeld's Strange Loop 2018 talk ('Tree-sitter — a new parsing system for programming tools') is the canonical primary exposition of the incremental GLR + error-recovery design as deployed in Atom and GitHub.com code navigation.

THREAD-SAFETY/MEMORY: 'Individual TSTree instances are not thread safe; you must copy a tree if you want to use it on multiple threads simultaneously', and 'Copying a syntax tree just entails incrementing an atomic reference count' (docs Advanced Parsing; api.h repeats the copy requirement). The Rust crate explicitly declares 'impl Send for Tree' and 'impl Sync for Tree' (docs.rs/tree-sitter, Tree page); TSParser is stateful — use one parser per thread. TSNode is a value type tied to its tree's lifetime.

LANGUAGE COVERAGE (R1): the official wiki 'List of parsers' enumerates roughly 900+ grammars; Rust (tree-sitter/tree-sitter-rust, ABI 15), Markdown (tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-markdown, ABI 15), JSON (ABI 14), TOML (ABI 14), YAML (ABI 14), and Bash (ABI 15) are all present. Adopters include Neovim, GNU Emacs, Helix, Zed, Lapce, and GitHub.com symbolic code navigation (Wikipedia). CRITICAL markdown caveat from its own README: it is a two-grammar design (block grammar, then inline grammar via ts_parser_set_included_ranges) and 'it is not recommended to use this parser where correctness is important. The main goal for this parser is to provide syntactical information for syntax highlighting', with 'still lots of inaccuracies in the output' (tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-markdown).

research.fit_assessment: R1 (parse every language) — STRONG: ~900+ grammars including all six named Oyatie formats; arbitrary customer-repo languages loadable as compiled C dylibs or sandboxed WASM grammars; ABI window (15, min-compatible 13) makes fleet pinning tractable. Caveat: grammar quality/perf varies per community grammar. R2 (content-addressed node identity) — FAILS NATIVELY, and this is the load-bearing gap: TSNode identity = process-local subtree pointer + byte ranges; stable only when a subtree is opportunistically reused; no content hash exists in the model. ADR-0517 (one-way door) already rejected tree-sitter on exactly this crux. Bridging requires an Oyatie-owned content-address overlay (hash = f(kind, field, child-hashes, token-bytes)) computed over the CST, with ts_tree_get_changed_ranges bounding re-hashing — feasible as an adapter concern, never as the trait's identity. R3 (incremental re-parse) — STRONG: this is tree-sitter's reason to exist; tree-edit + node-reuse gives edit-proportional work, third-party numbers show ~60 ms marginal cost for ~5.5k inserted lines and 73 ms full parse of a 5.8k-line file; interactive budget is comfortably met for code. Caveat: queries are NOT incrementally maintained — gate re-evaluation must be windowed over changed ranges by Oyatie code. R4 (error tolerance) — STRONG: cost-based GLR recovery emits queryable (ERROR)/(MISSING) nodes, proven on every-keystroke editor workloads; but recovery shape is an undocumented heuristic that can shift between releases, so gate findings near error regions need tolerance. R5 (AST doc-tracking) — WEAK ECOSYSTEM FIT: the flagship markdown grammar disclaims correctness ('not recommended... where correctness is important'), and tree-sitter produces per-file CSTs only — no cross-file edge model; stale_reference/broken_link/derived_doc_drift edges must be an Oyatie layer regardless. This matches W2's 'owned Rust + Markdown parser' scoping in HANDOFF §6.5. R6 (pattern gates + auto-fix) — GOOD for detection, PARTIAL for fix: S-expr queries with captures/fields/predicates are proven at hyperscale (GitHub, Neovim, Helix) for ADVISE/GATE-style pattern matching, but predicates run host-side (Rust binding), there are no cross-pattern joins or dataflow, and the engine has no rewrite facility — behavior-preserving AUTO-fix is an Oyatie-built rewriter over captures (ast-grep is the existence proof). R7 (Rust purity) — EXCEPTION REQUIRED AND SCOPE-SCALING: the core is C11 behind the tree-sitter Rust crate, and every grammar adds generated C plus often a hand-written scanner.c, so the C surface grows with language count — materially worse than the bounded aws-lc-rs precedent; ADR-0517 already rules bespoke Rust as the destination, so tree-sitter is at most the transitional impl, with an exception-ledger row covering core + each admitted grammar (WASM grammar sandboxing can shrink the trust surface). R8 (transitional impl behind WorkAreaTree) — WORKABLE WITH DISCIPLINE: the trait must speak the DESTINATION's shapes — content-addressed node ids, owned rowan-style green/red trees, Oyatie's query/finding contract — and must not leak TSNode, pointer ids, byte-range identity, tree-sitter's query dialect, or its host-side-predicate semantics; the adapter absorbs pointer→hash mapping, per-language ABI loading, and one-parser-per-thread. Cutover test per founder doctrine ('would this trait change at cutover?') passes only if identity and query semantics are defined by Oyatie, with tree-sitter strictly behind the port.
risks: Node-identity gap (R2): pointer-based, process-local, reuse-dependent ids mean any naive use of TSNode.id for locking or affected-set computation is unsound across parses/processes; the required content-hash overlay adds re-hashing cost and its correctness depends on Oyatie code, not tree-sitter. ADR-0517 is a one-way door rejecting tree-sitter as substrate — any adoption framed as anything other than an ADR-0510/0520 transitional adapter is a governance violation.

C surface scales per grammar (R7): core C11 runtime (~533 KB source) plus generated parser.c plus hand-written scanner.c for most nontrivial languages (Python indents, heredocs, YAML); the exception-ledger row is open-ended unless grammars are pinned and/or loaded as sandboxed WASM; this is qualitatively unlike the single bounded aws-lc-rs artifact already in third-party/.

Markdown correctness (R5): the canonical grammar's own README says it is 'not recommended... where correctness is important' and targets syntax highlighting; building the staleness gate family (stale_reference/broken_link/derived_doc_drift) on it risks false gates; an owned markdown parser (already the W2 plan) is the mitigation.

Error-recovery instability (R4/R6): recovery is an in-code cost heuristic (ERROR_COST_PER_SKIPPED_*) with no documented contract; tree shapes around syntax errors can change across releases, destabilizing gate findings and auto-fix anchors near in-progress agent edits; 'fragile' subtrees also defeat reuse, degrading incrementality exactly where agents edit.

Query-engine limits (R6/R3): predicates execute in the host binding, not the C core; no incremental query maintenance (re-run over changed ranges is DIY); no rewrite facility — the AUTO tier's behavior-preserving fixes are entirely Oyatie-built; complex anti-patterns needing name resolution or dataflow exceed query power and need a semantic layer.

Operational: grammar fleet management — per-grammar ABI levels (13–15 observed in the wild), backwards-but-not-forwards compatibility, and widely varying grammar quality/perf (Haskell needed a 50x fix) require a curated, pinned, benchmarked grammar registry; TSTree is not thread-safe without a (cheap, refcount) copy and TSParser is one-per-thread, constraining parallel gate-fleet design.

Evidence caveats: the 36x JavaParser comparison and Discussion #800 node-id guidance were captured at search-snippet level; owen.cafe returned HTTP 403 (title-level only); official docs publish no benchmark table, so Oyatie should run its own corpus benchmarks before relying on latency budgets.

research.summary: Tree-sitter is a mature, actively maintained C library with first-party Rust bindings (crate `tree-sitter` 0.26.9, May 2026, 23M+ downloads) that statically links its C core via cc/build.rs — a pattern Oyatie's buck2/reindeer setup already handles (third-party/fixups/aws-lc-sys precedent). All six required grammars exist as crates (TOML only via the community `tree-sitter-toml-ng` fork). It is excellent on incremental re-parse (R3) and query-based pattern gates (R6 detection), adequate on error tolerance (R4), but natively FAILS content-addressed node identity (R2) — node ids are pointer/identity-based, exactly the "node-identity crux" ADR-0517 cites when it founder-rules (one-way door) that tree-sitter reuse as destination is REJECTED and bespoke "tree-sitter-our-way, rowan-style" is the W2 destination. No serious safe-pure-Rust reimplementation exists (tree-sitter-c2rust is a mechanical unsafe transpile; Helix's tree-house is new bindings, not a reimpl; rust-analyzer's rowan is a different architecture whose content-interned green nodes are the structural precedent for the destination). The defensible role for tree-sitter in Oyatie is the ADR-0520/ADR-0510 transitional impl behind WorkAreaTree (trait not yet in code), with an adapter-side Merkle content-hash pass and an exception-ledger row for the C core, while the bespoke substrate is built to the same trait.

rust-analyzer chose rowan, not tree-sitter: rowan is a Roslyn-style green/red lossless tree where immutable green nodes are aggressively interned/deduplicated by content (in `1 + 1` the token `1` exists once with refcount 2) with a typed AST layer on top — this content-interning is the direct architectural precedent for ADR-0517's 'rowan-style, content-addressed' destination. matklad's documented reasoning (Resilient LL Parsing Tutorial): tree-sitter is GLR — it 'recognize[s] many complete valid small fragments... but might have trouble assembling them into incomplete larger fragments' (for `fn fib_rec(f1: u32,` it sees the parameter but not the function), whereas resilient LL 'naturally allows for incomplete large nodes'; he still pragmatically advises 'just use Tree-sitter' to get something working quickly. rust-analyzer's own syntax.md cites IntelliJ/Roslyn/Swift/Dart and never mentions tree-sitter [matklad.github.io/2023/05/21/resilient-ll-parsing-tutorial.html; rust-analyzer docs/book/src/contributing/syntax.md; github.com/rust-analyzer/rowan]

research.fit_assessment: R1 (parse every language): STRONG for the named six — all exist as crates from the tree-sitter or tree-sitter-grammars orgs (TOML only via the -ng community fork). For arbitrary customer-repo languages there are hundreds of community grammars of highly variable quality (difftastic had to normalize per-grammar inconsistencies; C++ lacks preprocessor fidelity). Static compiled-in grammars form a CLOSED set; runtime extension requires either Helix-style dylib loading (violates hermetic/distroless posture) or the `wasm` feature (adds wasmtime — heavy dep). Verdict: best-in-class breadth, but 'any repo' needs an explicit grammar-set governance decision. R2 (content-addressed node identity): NATIVE FAIL — node ids are pointer/identity-based and only conditionally stable across reparse; this is the exact crux ADR-0517 cites. Workaround is an adapter-side Merkle/content-hash post-pass over changed subtrees, which works but forfeits native incremental identity and creates dual-identity bookkeeping; rowan's content-interned green nodes are the proven pattern the bespoke destination should copy. R3 (incremental reparse): STRONG — incremental GLR with tree.edit() is tree-sitter's core design, proven at Zed scale on a background thread with snapshot isolation; interactive latency budget is comfortably met. R4 (error tolerance): ADEQUATE-WITH-CAVEAT — ERROR/MISSING nodes always yield a usable tree, but matklad's documented analysis shows GLR recovery recognizes small complete fragments while struggling to assemble incomplete LARGER constructs — and agent-authored in-progress code is precisely the incomplete-large-construct case. Acceptable for gates; weaker than resilient-LL for fine-grained mid-edit tooling. R5 (AST doc-tracking): PARTIAL — tree-sitter-md provides a solid block+inline markdown CST (links, references, headings as typed nodes); the cross-file stale_reference/broken_link/derived_doc_drift graph and file→ADR typed citation edges are an Oyatie-built layer ABOVE any parser, so tree-sitter neither blocks nor delivers this; it only supplies per-file trees. R6 (query language + auto-fix): STRONG for detection — the S-expression query language with captures/predicates is exactly the practice/anti-pattern gate shape (Zed, Neovim, and ast-grep all prove this at scale, and ast-grep is Rust-on-tree-sitter precedent for the rewrite layer). WEAK natively for auto-fix — trees are read-only; there is no rewrite API; behavior-preserving fixes must be implemented as span-anchored text edits + reparse verification (ast-grep's approach). R7 (Rust purity): FAILS natively — the C core behind Rust bindings requires an exception-ledger row; the aws-lc-rs/aws-lc-sys precedent (already in tree with reindeer fixups) makes this procedurally cheap. tree-sitter-c2rust avoids C linkage but is machine-generated unsafe Rust from a third-party fork — strictly worse on the doctrine's intent. Bespoke rowan-style remains the founder-ruled one-way-door destination (ADR-0517); tree-sitter is not the Firecracker-style proven-artifact adoption case here because the destination is already ruled. R8 (transitional impl behind WorkAreaTree): COMPATIBLE AND RECOMMENDED ROLE — WorkAreaTree has no Rust implementation yet, so the trait can be shaped for the OWNED destination now: expose content-addressed node identity (adapter computes Merkle hashes over the tree-sitter CST), typed-node kinds, query/match, span-anchored edits, and incremental-update semantics. The cutover review question ('would this trait change at cutover?') is answerable NO if the trait never leaks tree-sitter's pointer ids, ABI versions, Language handles, or query objects. Net: tree-sitter is the strongest available transitional impl for W2 (proven at Zed/Difftastic/Helix scale, buck2-tractable in this repo today), provided the adapter absorbs the identity-hash pass and the C-core exception is ledgered.
risks: Identity-layer cost: content-addressed node identity must be bolted on as an adapter-side Merkle pass; every incremental reparse needs re-hashing of changed subtrees plus dual bookkeeping (tree-sitter pointer id vs Oyatie content hash) — latency and complexity that the bespoke rowan-style destination eliminates natively; if this pass leaks into the WorkAreaTree trait shape, the cutover guarantee (ADR-0510/0520) is broken

Grammar ABI/version drift is a proven ecosystem pain: Helix built tree-house partly to chase the C 0.22→0.25 ABI as grammars adopted new ABIs, and Difftastic vendors grammars because of version-compat breakage (issue #891) — Oyatie would need to pin core+grammar versions in lockstep and treat upgrades as coordinated events

TOML grammar is the weak link: original crate abandoned, maintained only as community fork tree-sitter-toml-ng (~1 release/year, 335K downloads) — for a language central to the Rust/Cargo conformance ratchet

GLR error recovery underperforms resilient-LL on incomplete large constructs (matklad's documented `fn fib_rec(f1: u32,` example) — agent loops authoring in-progress code hit exactly this shape; gate findings on half-written functions may attach to ERROR nodes instead of usable typed nodes

R1 'any customer repo' vs hermeticity tension: statically compiled-in grammars are a closed set; the two runtime-extension mechanisms (dylib loading, wasmtime wasm grammars) respectively violate the distroless/hermetic posture and add a heavyweight dependency — requires an explicit ADR on the supported-grammar governance model

Rust-purity exception scope: the C core plus EVERY grammar crate is its own C compilation unit — the exception-ledger row(s) and buck2 fixups multiply per grammar added (mechanical but unbounded as customer languages grow)

No rewrite API: AUTO-tier behavior-preserving auto-fix (ADR-0519/0529/0531) must be built as span-anchored text edits + reparse + tree-equivalence verification on top; tree-sitter provides match sites only — the 5 AUTO safety proofs are entirely Oyatie's to construct

Query language ceiling: queries are purely syntactic (no name resolution, no types); practice gates needing semantic facts (unused import, dead code across files) will outgrow it, pushing logic into bespoke Rust passes regardless of substrate

Per-grammar CST inconsistency (difftastic's atom_nodes normalization problem): cross-language gates need a normalization layer because grammars disagree on node shapes for identical constructs — this layer is throwaway work at bespoke cutover unless deliberately designed into the WorkAreaTree adapter

Doctrine risk: ADR-0517 is a founder-ruled one-way door rejecting tree-sitter as substrate; any adoption MUST be framed strictly as the ADR-0520 transitional impl with a ledgered exception, or it contradicts accepted governance
sources: https://mitranim.com/posts/rant-tree-sitter-zed (independent critique: JS+C grammar toolchain, N*M complexity)

research.summary: Tree-sitter is the de-facto universal parsing substrate: ~650+ grammars, proven at GitHub scale (millions of repos, thousands of pushes/min), and adopted by Semgrep (30+ languages), CodeQL's Ruby extractor, Neovim, Zed, and Helix. Its four design goals map directly onto R1/R3/R4 (general, every-keystroke incremental, error-tolerant, dependency-free C11). But the ecosystem's chronic disease is version skew: still 0.x after 9+ years, grammar ABI breakage (13/14/15), breaking changes even within the same ABI number, and per-grammar quality variance (the markdown grammar — critical to R5 — explicitly disclaims correctness). Every serious production user converged on the same survival pattern Oyatie should adopt: pin grammar source revisions in a lockfile, compile hermetically with one toolchain, build your own semantic/identity layer on top, and never depend on ecosystem-distributed binaries. The cautionary tale is GitHub itself: it built and then archived TWO semantic layers above tree-sitter (semantic in Haskell; stack-graphs archived 2025-09-09) while the tree-sitter parsing layer underneath survived both. Verdict: dependable infrastructure for R1/R3/R4/R6-matching, but R2 (content-addressed identity), R5 (markdown accuracy), and R6-rewrite are bespoke Rust layers Oyatie must own, and R7 requires an exception-ledger row for the C core plus per-grammar C/C++ scanners — exactly the ADR-0510 transient-impl-behind-WorkAreaTree shape.
facts: GitHub scale: the stack-graphs paper (Creager, arXiv 2211.01224) states GitHub hosts 'millions of repositories, containing petabytes of total code, implemented in hundreds of different programming languages, and receiving thousands of pushes per minute'; stack graph construction is file-incremental (each file's subgraph built in isolation, merged at query time) to avoid reanalyzing unchanged files.

Why tree-sitter alone wasn't enough at GitHub: tree-sitter produces concrete syntax trees only; GitHub added a declarative graph-construction DSL (tree-sitter-graph stanzas) and the stack-graphs framework on top to model name binding, scoping, shadowing, and cross-file references (github.blog 'Introducing stack graphs').

GitHub precise code navigation shipped for Python (GA announced Dec 2021) and all TypeScript repositories (changelog 2024-03-14); the github/stack-graphs languages/ tree carries grammars for Python, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript. Search-based code navigation uses tree-sitter tag queries and covers 19 languages (github/code-navigation).

github/semantic (Haskell, generated per-language Haskell syntax types from tree-sitter grammars; supported Ruby/JS/TS/Python/Go/PHP/Java/JSON et al.) is archived: 'This repository is no longer supported or updated by GitHub.' Its successor github/stack-graphs was ALSO archived on September 9, 2025 with the same notice — GitHub abandoned two successive semantic layers while the tree-sitter parsing layer survived both.

CodeQL's Ruby extractor is built in Rust on tree-sitter (ruby/extractor/Cargo.toml): a tool reads the grammar's node-types.json and mechanically generates the CodeQL DB schema and TRAP extraction, a process GitHub calls 'completely language-agnostic'; the same tooling was repointed at the ERB grammar for Rails. CodeQL's compiled-language extractors remain compiler-integrated, showing tree-sitter is the syntactic tier, not the semantic tier (github.blog 'Code scanning and Ruby').

Semgrep parses 30+ languages via tree-sitter: grammars are forked/extended in ocaml-tree-sitter-semgrep to add metavariables ($FOO) and ellipsis (...) as grammar rules, OCaml parser code is generated, then a hand-written per-language translator converts each CST into Semgrep's single generic AST (AST_generic) that rules match against. Documented pain points: 'Avoiding parsing conflicts is the trickiest part', upstream grammar incompleteness, scanner.c mismatches, and segfaults in C bindings (docs.semgrep.dev/contributing/adding-a-language).

Neovim grammar version-skew: recurring nvim-treesitter failures of the form 'This version of Tree-sitter can only generate parsers with ABI version 13 - 14, not 15' and runtime-vs-library ABI mismatches; the nvim-treesitter 'main' branch is a 'full, incompatible, rewrite' that pins exact parser revisions (parser.lua) and requires tree-sitter-cli >= 0.26.1, bumping a parser revision only when query tests pass (nvim-treesitter README, issues #8147/#8151).

ABI fragility evidence: identical Emacs 29.2 builds support ABI 15 on macOS but only ABI 14 on Windows ('ABI version mismatch (library: 15, runtime: 14)'), and 'ABI 14 has internal breaking changes between tree-sitter 0.20.x and 0.21.x' — same ABI number, incompatible behavior (cottontailia.github.io). WASM grammars built with tree-sitter-cli 0.20.x are incompatible with web-tree-sitter 0.26.x (tree-sitter issue #5171). Headers historically did not expose ABI version (issue #3925).

Versioning history: tree-sitter is still pre-1.0 after ~9 years (latest v0.26.9, May 19 2026; 1.0 checklist issue #930 open). ABI 15 was introduced in v0.25.0 (adds language name/version, supertype info, reserved words to parsers; requires tree-sitter.json). The library is backwards-compatible with grammars of ABI >= 13 but not forwards-compatible.

Ecosystem breadth: the official wiki lists ~650+ parsers covering programming languages plus markdown, JSON, TOML, YAML, HCL, bash, SQL, Dockerfile, etc.; a minority are maintained by the tree-sitter org, the majority by community individuals/orgs with wide quality variance (tree-sitter wiki List-of-parsers; dcreager.net counted 40+ in 2021 — ~16x growth).

Markdown grammar caveat (direct R5 impact): tree-sitter-markdown is community-maintained (tree-sitter-grammars org), uses a two-grammar block+inline design requiring a second parse via ts_parser_set_included_ranges, and its README states 'it is not recommended to use this parser where correctness is important' and admits 'still lots of inaccuracies in the output' — its stated goal is syntax highlighting.

WASM sandbox story: the core library has a compile-time wasmtime integration to load .wasm grammars; Zed runs only lexing (the hand-written external-scanner code) inside the WASM sandbox while marshaling the static parse tables into native memory, because 'parsing is driven entirely by static data' and the sandbox 'makes it impossible for extensions to crash' the host (zed.dev language-extensions-part-1). Wasmtime itself is Rust.

Node identity (R2 gap): docs.rs tree_sitter::Node::id — 'Within a given syntax tree, no two nodes have the same id'; an id persists across an incremental re-parse only if the subtree is reused, and 'a node not marked as having changes does not guarantee it was reused.' Node ids are session-local pointers, NOT content-addressed and NOT stable across processes — a Merkle-style structural hash layer must be built above the tree.

Error tolerance (R4): stated design goal 'Robust enough to provide useful results even in the presence of syntax errors'; the API exposes is_error, has_error, and is_missing ('Missing nodes are inserted by the parser in order to recover from certain kinds of syntax errors'). Recovery quality is heuristic and varies per grammar.

Design goals confirming R1/R3/R7 shape: 'General enough to parse any programming language', 'Fast enough to parse on every keystroke in a text editor', 'Dependency-free so that the runtime library (which is written in pure C11) can be embedded in any application' — i.e., the runtime is C by design, with tier-1 Rust bindings maintained in-repo; no production pure-Rust runtime port exists.

Query language (R6): S-expression patterns with captures and predicates, used in production by GitHub tags extraction, Neovim highlighting, and Zed. It is match-only — no rewrite capability; Semgrep and ast-grep (a Rust precedent) each built their own pattern-extension and autofix/rewrite layers above tree-sitter.
research.fit_assessment:
R1 (parse every language) — STRONG FIT, best available. ~650 grammars cover Rust, markdown, JSON, TOML, YAML, bash, and essentially any customer-repo language; Semgrep (30+ langs), CodeQL-Ruby, and GitHub's 19-language tags pipeline prove production viability for exactly Oyatie's syntactic-analysis tier. No alternative offers comparable breadth; building per-language parsers bespoke is years of work GitHub/Semgrep both declined. Caveat: long-tail grammar quality varies; the conformance ratchet needs a per-grammar admission test (parse-rate corpus check, the Semgrep pattern) before a language is GATE-tier rather than ADVISE-tier.
R2 (content-addressed node identity) — GAP, bespoke layer required. Node ids are session-local and reuse-dependent, not content hashes. Oyatie must build a Merkle structural-hash layer (kind + normalized span content + child hashes) in owned Rust above the tree; tree-sitter supplies the right inputs (stable structure, byte ranges, changed-subtree flags as cache hints, not guarantees). This is the same 'tree-sitter alone is not enough' boundary GitHub hit; the identity layer is the WorkAreaTree value-add and feeds buck2 content addressing naturally.
R3 (incremental re-parse) — STRONG FIT. Core design goal (every-keystroke), ts_tree_edit + subtree reuse, file-incremental at GitHub scale. Meets interactive agent-loop budgets.
R4 (error tolerance) — STRONG FIT with variance. ERROR/MISSING/has_error are first-class; agent-authored partial code yields usable trees. Recovery quality is unspecified heuristic behavior that differs per grammar — gates must treat subtrees under ERROR nodes as advisory.
R5 (AST doc-tracking) — VIABLE, but markdown is the weak link: the community markdown grammar explicitly disclaims correctness and requires a two-pass block/inline parse. Recommendation: drive staleness/broken-link/derived-drift edges from a spec-conformant pure-Rust CommonMark parser (e.g., pulldown-cmark — also removes a C surface) normalized into the same typed-node model, with tree-sitter handling the code side and language-injection ranges for embedded snippets; or pin and conformance-test the grammar before trusting it in a GATE.
R6 (query/pattern + auto-fix) — HALF FIT. The S-expression query language with predicates is production-grade for practice/anti-pattern MATCHING (GitHub tags, nvim, Zed all run on it). It is match-only: behavior-preserving auto-fix and metavariable/ellipsis-style authoring are owned layers (Semgrep forked every grammar to get them; ast-grep is the Rust-native precedent to study under proven-patterns doctrine).
R7 (Rust purity) — EXCEPTION-LEDGER ROW REQUIRED. The runtime is pure C11 by design; grammars are generated C plus optional hand-written C/C++ scanners; the tier-1 Rust crate is FFI over that core (aws-lc-rs precedent applies directly). Scope the ledger row to include each admitted grammar's external scanner, not just libtree-sitter. Mitigation path: wasmtime-sandboxed grammar loading (Zed pattern — scanner code confined to a Rust-hosted sandbox, parse tables native). Bespoke-Rust destination: a pure-Rust runtime+grammar story is the cutover target; none exists today, so this is the classic transitional impl.
R8 (stable WorkAreaTree trait) — SUPPORTED AND MANDATORY. The skew evidence dictates the adapter discipline: vendor grammar SOURCES at pinned revisions, compile hermetically under buck2 with one pinned tree-sitter toolchain (this neutralizes the entire ABI-skew failure class, which only bites consumers of ecosystem-distributed binaries — nvim-treesitter's lockfile ratchet is the proven pattern), and never let TSNode lifetimes, ABI numbers, or query handles leak through the trait. The trait should speak destination concepts only: content-addressed node ids, typed edges (file→ADR citation), incremental edit sessions, pattern handles, fix plans. Under that shape the trait does not change at cutover to a pure-Rust or wasm-hosted backend.
risks: Perpetual pre-1.0: tree-sitter is 0.x after 9+ years (v0.26.9, May 2026; 1.0 checklist still open) with breaking changes in minor releases and documented incompatibilities within the SAME ABI number (0.20.x vs 0.21.x) — semver cannot be trusted; only hermetic source pinning of {core, CLI, every grammar} as one lockstep unit is safe.

Grammar ABI skew is the ecosystem's dominant operational failure (Neovim issue volume, Emacs 29.2 macOS-vs-Windows ABI 15/14 split, web-tree-sitter wasm incompatibility). Any path where grammars are built by a different toolchain than the runtime — including customer-supplied or ecosystem-prebuilt artifacts — reintroduces it; the universal pipeline must compile all grammars itself.

Quality/governance variance across ~650 mostly community grammars; the markdown grammar (load-bearing for R5 staleness gates) explicitly states it should not be used 'where correctness is important'. Untested long-tail grammars can silently mis-parse customer code, corrupting affected-set computation and gate verdicts — per-grammar conformance corpora and parse-rate thresholds are required admission gates.

Hand-written C/C++ external scanners in community grammars are arbitrary unsafe code inside the pipeline: memory-unsafety (Semgrep reports segfaults) and a supply-chain surface. The R7 exception-ledger row must enumerate per-grammar scanners; wasmtime sandboxing (Zed pattern) is the mitigation for untrusted/customer grammars but adds a wasm toolchain dependency.

Semantic-layer abandonment precedent: GitHub archived both github/semantic and github/stack-graphs (2025-09-09). Everything above raw parsing — identity hashing, typed doc-edges, pattern/fix layers — has no durable upstream; Oyatie owns it forever. This matches bespoke-Rust doctrine but is real headcount, and stack-graphs/tree-sitter-graph crates are now unmaintained dependencies to avoid.

R2 identity is entirely bespoke: incremental-reuse node ids are explicitly non-guaranteed ('not marked as having changes does not guarantee it was reused'), so content hashing must be recomputed structurally, and hash stability across grammar-version bumps (node kinds can be renamed by grammar updates) must be part of the lockfile ratchet's test surface.

Query language is match-only and grammar-version-coupled: queries reference grammar node names, so every grammar bump can break gate queries (the exact failure nvim-treesitter's CI exists to catch) — gate/query test suites must run in the same ratchet that admits grammar updates; auto-fix (R6) requires building or adopting a rewrite engine (ast-grep precedent) on top.

research.summary: Survey of tree-sitter alternatives for Oyatie W2 (owned AST substrate behind WorkAreaTree, per ADR-0517/0520/0521 and HANDOFF.md §6.5). Conclusion: no single off-the-shelf alternative covers R1-R8; the evidence supports a composition that matches ADR-0517's "tree-sitter-our-way, rowan-style" ruling. (a) rowan+ungrammar is the strongest tree-layer fit: pure Rust, lossless CST, green nodes are immutable, structurally-shared, content-identified (Roslyn/Swift-libsyntax lineage; Biome ships a production fork) — but it is a tree library, not a parser, and has no multi-language grammar ecosystem. (b) chumsky/winnow/pest are per-language handwritten frameworks: winnow is proven at Cargo scale (toml_edit), chumsky has real but limited error recovery, pest has neither recovery nor incrementality; none offer incremental reparse, so R3 fails across the category. (c) Stack graphs (GitHub, built on scope-graph theory from TU Delft/Spoofax) solve reference resolution above parsing — the right blueprint for R5 typed citation edges — but github/stack-graphs was archived 2025-09-09; adopt concepts, not code. (d) SWC/oxc/Ruff-style handwritten parsers are the speed and error-recovery champions (oxc ~3x swc, 5x Biome) but cost man-years per language, failing R1 universality; Biome (handwritten resilient parsers emitting a rowan-fork CST) is the closest existing union of (a)+(d) and the best production template for Oyatie's first-party languages. (e) difftastic is not a parser substrate; it demonstrates the consume-tree-sitter-grammars-then-lower-to-an-owned-uniform-IR adapter pattern that R8 prescribes, including an explicit degraded fallback mode. (f) A reimplemented pure-Rust runtime consuming tree-sitter grammar artifacts is genuinely feasible and is the highest-leverage W2 path: tree-sitter's table generator already exists as a Rust library (tree-sitter-generate, MIT), lezer proves a small team can reimplement the incremental-GLR runtime in another language, and tree-sitter-c2rust proves the runtime is mechanically transpilable to (unsafe) Rust today; the hard blocker is external scanners — bash, YAML, and markdown grammars require hand-written C scanner.c (arbitrary code, not language-agnostic data), so each supported language with a scanner needs a Rust port or an exception-ledger row. No complete independent safe-Rust runtime consuming tree-sitter artifacts exists yet; Oyatie would be first. (g) For the doc-tracking lane, comrak (Rust port of GitHub's cmark-gfm, full AST with sourcepos, used by docs.rs/crates.io) is the correctness-grade choice; tree-sitter-markdown's own README warns it is "not recommended to use this parser where correctness is important," which disqualifies it for R5 gates; pulldown-cmark (rustdoc/mdBook) is fast but event-based, not a lossless tree. Recommended shape: rowan-style content-addressed green/red tree as the ONE owned tree type; owned Rust incremental-GLR runtime fed by tree-sitter grammar.json tables for the universal lane; handwritten resilient parsers (Biome pattern) for Rust; comrak-compliance markdown adapter; tree-sitter-C-via-bindings or tree-sitter-c2rust as the ADR-0510 transitional impl behind WorkAreaTree with an aws-lc-rs-style exception-ledger row.
facts: rowan green trees are fully immutable with structural sharing and interning; identical subtrees are deduplicated to the same Arc<Node> ('a single token for 1 with ref count 2'), i.e. green-node identity is content-based — but green trees 'just can't differentiate between' two identical occurrences; positional identity is added by the red SyntaxNode layer (rust-analyzer docs/book syntax.md, https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/blob/master/docs/book/src/contributing/syntax.md)

rowan's red/green design derives from Roslyn (Microsoft) and Swift libsyntax; rust-analyzer pairs it with a hand-written parser; ungrammar is a DSL describing only the SHAPE of the CST ('producing a parser is an explicit non-goal') used to generate typed AST accessors (https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rowan, https://rust-analyzer.github.io//blog/2020/10/24/introducing-ungrammar.html)

Biome's parser infrastructure is an internal fork of rowan (biome_rowan); its handwritten parsers are error-resilient and recoverable by design, emitting lossless CSTs with 'Bogus' nodes for malformed code — production proof that rowan-style CST + handwritten resilient parsers works outside rust-analyzer (https://biomejs.dev/internals/architecture/, https://docs.rs/biome_rowan)

chumsky supports first-class error recovery (partial ASTs from broken input) via recursive-descent combinators, but recovery has known limits (no recursive recovery) and there is no incremental parsing support (https://github.com/zesterer/chumsky, https://blog.romamik.com/blog/2025-09-18-chumsky-recovery/, https://blog.jsbarretto.com/post/parser-combinators-and-error-recovery)

winnow was created by epage specifically because toml_edit's parser was too slow for Cargo — it now powers TOML parsing inside Cargo, an at-scale Rust-toolchain precedent for combinator parsing of data formats; error recovery and incrementality are DIY (https://epage.github.io/blog/2023/02/winnow-toml-edit-combine-nom/)

pest has no error-recovery story (Result returns a single Error; discussion #711 'Continuing on errors' is open-ended) and no incremental parsing; both are deferred aspirations for pest3 (https://github.com/pest-parser/pest/discussions/711, https://github.com/pest-parser/pest/discussions/885)

github/stack-graphs was archived by the owner on September 9, 2025 and is read-only; stack graphs (Creager, arXiv 2211.01224) extend TU Delft scope-graph theory (Neron/Tolmach/Visser/Wachsmuth, ESOP 2015) and powered GitHub Precise Code Navigation; construction rules are written in the tree-sitter-graph DSL on top of tree-sitter grammars — it complements parsing, it does not replace it (https://github.com/github/stack-graphs, https://github.blog/open-source/introducing-stack-graphs/, https://pl.ewi.tudelft.nl/research/projects/scope-graphs/)

oxc's handwritten recursive-descent parser with arena-allocated AST is ~3x faster than swc and 5x faster than Biome (Biome builds a costlier CST), with sophisticated error recovery for IDE use — per-language handwritten parsers are the speed/recovery champions but each is a major project, so the approach cannot satisfy R1 universality (https://github.com/oxc-project/bench-javascript-parser-written-in-rust, https://oxc.rs/docs/contribute/parser)

difftastic consumes tree-sitter C grammars via bindings, lowers every parse tree into its own simplified uniform Syntax representation, then diffs with Dijkstra; it falls back to line-oriented diffing when limits are exceeded — a working template for 'foreign grammars behind an owned IR' plus explicit degraded modes (https://github.com/Wilfred/difftastic, https://www.wilfred.me.uk/blog/2022/09/06/difftastic-the-fantastic-diff/)

tree-sitter's CLI (including grammar loading and parse-table building) is written in Rust and published as a reusable MIT library crate tree-sitter-generate (generate_parser_for_grammar, load_grammar_file); only the runtime libtree-sitter is C — the table-generation half of an owned pure-Rust pipeline already exists in Rust (https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/5-implementation.html, https://docs.rs/tree-sitter-generate/latest/tree_sitter_generate/)

tree-sitter external scanners are hand-written C (src/scanner.c) and per tree-sitter docs 'must be implemented in C (as non-C implementations are no longer supported)'; YAML, bash, and markdown grammars all depend on them for indentation/context-sensitivity — so tree-sitter grammar artifacts are NOT purely language-agnostic data; the scanner is arbitrary code per grammar (https://tree-sitter.github.io/tree-sitter/creating-parsers/4-external-scanners.html, https://deepwiki.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-yaml)

tree-sitter-c2rust (shadaj) is a fork of tree-sitter whose C runtime is automatically transpiled to Rust via c2rust (no libc, builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown; v0.25.2 on crates.io, tracking upstream 0.25); it proves the runtime is mechanically portable to Rust, but the output is unsafe transpiled Rust, not an owned safe-Rust implementation (https://github.com/shadaj/tree-sitter-c2rust, https://crates.io/crates/tree-sitter-c2rust)

lezer (lezer-parser/lr, Marijn Haverbeke) is an independent incremental GLR runtime 'heavily influenced by tree-sitter' and the Wagner/Graham incremental-parsing papers, written from scratch in JavaScript for CodeMirror 6 — existence proof that a small team can own a tree-sitter-class incremental error-recovering runtime in another language; note lezer defines its own grammar format rather than consuming tree-sitter artifacts (https://lezer.codemirror.net/docs/guide/, https://github.com/lezer-parser/lr)

No complete independent safe-Rust runtime that consumes tree-sitter grammar artifacts was found; the closest existing art is tree-sitter-c2rust (mechanical transpile, consumes real grammars) and lezer (independent reimplementation, own grammar format); rust-sitter builds on tree-sitter-c2rust for grammar definition in Rust macros (https://github.com/hydro-project/rust-sitter, https://www.shadaj.me/writing/introducing-rust-sitter)

Helix replaced upstream tree-sitter Rust bindings with its own tree-house crate (helix-editor/tree-house) to fix correctness bugs in highlighting/injections over the C runtime — precedent that even committed tree-sitter consumers end up owning a robustness layer above the C library (https://github.com/helix-editor/tree-house, https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/pull/12972)

tree-sitter-markdown's own README states 'there are still lots of inaccuracies in the output' and it is 'not recommended to use this parser where correctness is important'; it requires a two-pass block-then-inline parse via ts_parser_set_included_ranges and a C external scanner — disqualifying for R5 correctness-gating (https://github.com/tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-markdown)

comrak is a 100% CommonMark + GFM compatible Rust port of cmark-gfm (GitHub's markdown C library) producing a full AST with source positions, used by docs.rs/crates.io; pulldown-cmark (used by rustdoc/cargo doc and mdBook) is faster but event-based — no AST by default, offsets only via into_offset_iter (https://github.com/kivikakk/comrak, https://github.com/pulldown-cmark/pulldown-cmark)

Unison is the at-scale precedent for content-addressed AST identity: every definition is identified by a hash of its syntax tree (structure, not names/formatting), stored in an append-only content-addressed code database, yielding perfect incremental compilation and rename-immunity — the same properties R2 needs for work-area hashing and affected-set computation (https://www.unison-lang.org/docs/the-big-idea/)

research.fit_assessment: Against R1-R8, no alternative passes alone; the evidence converges on a layered composition consistent with ADR-0517's pre-existing one-way ruling. R1 (every language): only the tree-sitter grammar ecosystem covers arbitrary customer-repo languages; rowan, chumsky/winnow/pest, and SWC/oxc-style parsers all require per-language hand work; difftastic and lezer show the ecosystem-reuse and runtime-reimplementation halves are separately proven. Option (f) — owned Rust runtime consuming tree-sitter grammar.json via the already-Rust tree-sitter-generate table pipeline — is the only R1-compatible path to an owned substrate, with the explicit caveat that external scanners (bash, YAML, markdown, ~half the important grammars) are per-grammar C code requiring Rust ports, not reusable data. R2 (content-addressed node identity): rowan's interned green trees are natively content-addressed (same structure = same node), the exact 'rowan-style' ADR-0517 names; Unison is the at-scale precedent; tree-sitter itself cannot provide this (confirmed by ADR-0517's node-identity crux). Caveat: green identity alone conflates identical occurrences — WorkAreaTree ids must hash content + path (red-layer) for claim-locking. R3 (incremental): tree-sitter and lezer are the only proven incremental designs surveyed; rowan/rust-analyzer has only block-level reparse; combinator frameworks have none. An owned runtime must implement Wagner-Graham incrementality — the genuinely hard part of (f). R4 (error tolerance): tree-sitter recovery is built-in; Biome/oxc prove handwritten resilient parsing; chumsky partial; pest fails. R5 (doc-tracking): comrak is the only correctness-grade markdown AST (tree-sitter-markdown self-disqualifies); stack/scope graphs are the right model for typed reference/citation edges but the GitHub implementation is archived — adopt the theory (ESOP 2015 scope graphs) into the owned substrate. R6 (query/pattern + auto-fix): tree-sitter queries and ast-grep style matching prove the pattern-language model; an owned rowan-style tree supports typed-node queries (Biome analyzer precedent); behavior-preserving rewrites need the lossless CST that rowan/Biome provide and oxc-style ASTs do not. R7 (Rust purity): rowan/ungrammar/comrak/chumsky/winnow are pure Rust; tree-sitter C runtime (whether via bindings, Helix tree-house-style wrapper, or unsafe-transpiled tree-sitter-c2rust) needs an exception-ledger row on the aws-lc-rs precedent; per-grammar scanner.c files are additional ledger rows until ported. R8 (transitional impl behind stable interface): the difftastic lower-to-owned-IR pattern and Helix tree-house wrapper show adapters absorbing tree-sitter cleanly; WorkAreaTree must expose Oyatie-computed content hashes, owned node kinds, and owned query semantics — never tree-sitter node ids or TSQuery — so the W2 cutover from the transitional C-backed adapter to the owned runtime does not change the trait. Net: destination = rowan-style content-addressed green/red tree + owned Rust incremental-GLR runtime consuming tree-sitter grammar tables (scanner ports per language) + handwritten resilient parsers for first-party Rust + comrak-compliance markdown adapter; transition = tree-sitter-C (bindings or c2rust) behind WorkAreaTree with ledger rows.
risks: External scanners break the 'grammar artifacts are language-agnostic data' premise of option (f): bash, YAML, and markdown grammars all require hand-written C scanner.c, and tree-sitter docs state non-C scanner implementations are no longer supported — every scanner-bearing language costs a Rust port or a standing C exception-ledger row, and the porting burden scales with customer-language count (R1 vs R7 tension).

Wagner-Graham incremental parsing plus tree-sitter-grade error recovery is the research-hard 20% of an owned runtime; tree-sitter and lezer each took years of expert effort — W2 schedule risk if incrementality (R3) is treated as a quick follow-on rather than a core deliverable.

tree-sitter grammar quality is uneven: tree-sitter-markdown's maintainers explicitly warn against correctness-critical use, and most community grammars target editor highlighting, not gating — running conformance ratchets (R5/R6 GATE tier) on unaudited grammars risks false findings; per-grammar conformance audits or a degraded ADVISE-only mode for unaudited languages is needed (difftastic's line-diff fallback is the precedent for explicit degraded modes).

rowan green-node content identity conflates identical occurrences (the docs are explicit that green trees cannot distinguish two copies of 'x + 2'); if WorkAreaTree node identity uses content hash alone, claim-time locking and affected-set computation will alias distinct work areas — identity must be (content_hash, path/parent-chain) pairs, which should be locked into the W1 trait now.

github/stack-graphs is archived (2025-09-09, read-only): no upstream maintenance, so any reference-resolution layer must treat it as a paper-plus-archived-reference-implementation, not a dependency; budget for owning scope-graph machinery if R5 typed citation edges grow into cross-file name resolution.

tree-sitter-c2rust is a single-maintainer fork producing unsafe mechanically-transpiled Rust that lags upstream releases — acceptable only as a short transitional adapter; long-term reliance contradicts the safe-Rust doctrine and trades a well-fuzzed C codebase for less-audited unsafe Rust without gaining memory safety.

rowan upstream is in low-activity maintenance mode under the rust-analyzer org (Biome and cstree both forked rather than contributed) — per the proven-patterns-reimplement doctrine Oyatie should expect to own its rowan-style tree implementation outright rather than depend on upstream rowan, mirroring Biome's fork decision.

Combinator-framework lock-in risk for the structured-data lane: winnow/chumsky parsers for TOML/JSON/YAML deliver no incrementality and idiosyncratic recovery; if they are admitted as permanent first-party parsers rather than adapters behind WorkAreaTree, R3 and uniform R2 hashing degrade for exactly the config formats the conformance ratchet reads most often.

Markdown spec drift: comrak tracks cmark-gfm (GitHub's dialect); CommonMark and GFM diverge and evolve, so R5 staleness gates must pin a spec version in the gate contract or doc-tracking findings will shift under dependency upgrades.

ADR-0517 is door:one-way (own the parser); any W2 plan that quietly hardens the transitional tree-sitter adapter into the destination (the common fate of 'temporary' parsers) violates the ADR — the cutover trigger and parity proof (e.g., byte-identical trees + hash stability on a corpus) should be specified in the W2 IP up front, per the ADR-0510 transitional-impl pattern.

prescription.ruling: ADOPT TREE-SITTER AS THE TRANSITIONAL IMPL ONLY (ADR-0510/0520 lane), for the CODE/UNIVERSAL lane (Rust + the ~900-grammar customer-repo long tail), behind the WorkAreaTree port; the bespoke rowan-style content-addressed substrate remains the founder-ruled one-way-door DESTINATION (ADR-0517), NOT permanent adoption. This is a HYBRID by lane, not a single backend. RATIONALE: (1) ADR-0517 is door:one-way, founder-ruled 2026-06-08, and already rejected tree-sitter AS THE SUBSTRATE on exactly two grounds the research re-confirms unanimously — minimal-deps doctrine and the content-addressed node-identity crux (TSNode.id is a process-local subtree pointer + byte ranges, stable only on opportunistic reuse, never content-addressed, no hash anywhere in the model). Re-ruling tree-sitter as the destination would reverse a one-way door; that is out of scope. (2) But ADR-0520 rules every substrate layer is 'transitional-impl-behind-a-stable-interface, none blocking', which is the legitimate lane the research (all four reports) and founder's 'consider tree-sitter' direction converge on. (3) The proven-patterns doctrine's adopt-the-proven-Rust-ARTIFACT exception (Firecracker case) does NOT apply: tree-sitter's artifact is a C core plus per-grammar generated C plus hand-written C scanner.c — an OPEN-ENDED C surface that scales with language count, qualitatively unlike the single bounded aws-lc-rs artifact; so it cannot be the destination, only the bridge. (4) R2 is the decisive crux and the founder's framing question — 'does identity-on-top-of-tree-sitter satisfy R2 without forking it?' — answers YES, AS AN ADAPTER CONCERN, NO, AS A SUBSTITUTE FOR THE DESTINATION: the content-addressed identity layer is OURS regardless of parser choice (Merkle hash = f(owned_kind, field, child-hashes, normalized-token-bytes) computed over the CST, re-hashing bounded by ts_tree_get_changed_ranges, occurrence-disambiguated by path/parent-chain per rowan's documented green-node-conflation caveat). This overlay is unforked (no tree-sitter source changes), satisfies R2 functionally for W2, but is bolt-on cost (dual bookkeeping: pointer-id vs content-hash, re-hash per edit) that the rowan-style destination eliminates natively — so it justifies the bridge, never cancels the cutover. (5) DECISIVE LANE SPLIT the research forces: the MARKDOWN/DOC-TRACKING lane (R5, AMENDMENT-10 authority/citation edges) must NOT ride tree-sitter-markdown — its own README says 'not recommended where correctness is important' and Oyatie already ships pulldown-cmark in third-party/fixups/; use a correctness-grade pure-Rust CommonMark/GFM AST (comrak, cmark-gfm-parity, full sourcepos) for the doc lane from day one. That lane is ALSO the governance-load-bearing one (AMENDMENT 10) and must lead W2. WHERE THE RESEARCH DISAGREES: report 4 argues the highest-leverage path is an owned pure-Rust runtime consuming tree-sitter grammar.json tables via the already-Rust tree-sitter-generate crate (lezer proves a small team can reimplement the incremental-GLR runtime; tree-sitter-c2rust proves mechanical transpilability) — this is genuinely attractive and accelerates the DESTINATION, but its hard blocker (external scanners are per-grammar hand-written C, non-C 'no longer supported', and bash/YAML/markdown all need them) means it is NOT a day-one shortcut and does not change the transitional ruling; it is the recommended SHAPE of the eventual bespoke build, captured as an open question. Reports 1-3 are unanimous that tree-sitter is a strong R1/R3/R4/R6-detection transitional adapter and a native R2/R5 fail — no material disagreement there. NET: adopt transitionally for code, bespoke-from-day-one for markdown/doc-tracking, build the owned identity layer ON TOP regardless, hold the bespoke rowan-style runtime as the one-way-door destination with numeric cutover triggers.
prescription.workareatree_port_shape: WorkAreaTree must speak ONLY the OWNED DESTINATION's vocabulary so the C-backed tree-sitter adapter and the future bespoke rowan-style runtime are interchangeable impls with ZERO trait change at cutover. It must NEVER leak TSNode, the `const void *id` pointer, TSTree lifetimes, ABI version numbers, TSQuery objects, tree-sitter's S-expression query dialect, host-side-predicate semantics, byte-range-as-identity, or per-grammar Language handles. Required surface: (1) NODE IDENTITY = content-addressed NodeId computed by US — a Merkle hash over (owned_node_kind, field_label, ordered child NodeIds, normalized leaf bytes), disambiguated for identical occurrences by a stable path/parent-chain key (rowan green-nodes conflate identical subtrees per its own docs; the red-layer path is what claim-locking and affected-set need) — feeding the buck2/RBE content-address and the single work-area hash (ADR-0517); identity is DEFINED BY OYATIE, never by the parser. (2) OWNED NODE-KIND taxonomy — a normalized cross-language kind enum (difftastic's atom_nodes problem: grammars disagree on identical constructs), so the adapter maps tree-sitter kinds INTO our taxonomy; the bespoke runtime emits it natively. (3) TYPED CROSS-FILE EDGES as first-class — file->ADR citation, stale_reference / unreachable_doc / broken_link / derived_doc_drift (R5, AMENDMENT 10) — NOT per-file CSTs only; tree-sitter gives per-file trees, so this edge graph is an Oyatie layer above ANY parser and lives in the trait shape now. (4) INCREMENTAL EDIT SESSIONS — apply(edit) -> changed-NodeId-set, modeling edit-proportional reparse + bounded re-hash; semantics defined by us, not by ts_tree_edit. (5) OWNED QUERY/PATTERN handles returning our Finding contract (ADR-0528) with the AUTO/ADVISE/GATE tier as data (ADR-0519/0529) — never raw TSQuery captures. (6) ERROR-TOLERANT typed nodes — owned Error/Missing/Partial node kinds (R4) with a tolerance contract, since tree-sitter's recovery shape is an undocumented heuristic that shifts across releases. (7) BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING FIX PLANs (span-anchored edits + reparse-verify; tree-sitter has no rewrite API) for the AUTO tier's 5 safety proofs (ADR-0519/0530/0531). Cutover test (founder doctrine 'would this trait change at cutover?'): PASSES iff every one of these is Oyatie-defined and the adapter — not the trait — absorbs pointer->hash mapping, per-grammar ABI loading, kind normalization, one-parser-per-thread, and recovery-shape tolerance.
cutover_criteria: IDENTITY-OVERLAY COST WALL: the adapter-side Merkle re-hash + dual-bookkeeping (TSNode-pointer-id <-> Oyatie content-hash) on incremental reparse exceeds the interactive agent-loop latency budget at p99 (proposed starting threshold: > 50 ms marginal re-hash on a representative 5k-line edit, measured on the production corpus, re-ratified-not-silently-changed per ADR-0510 discipline) — i.e. the bolt-on identity tax the rowan-style destination eliminates natively becomes the bottleneck.

C-SURFACE-PER-GRAMMAR LEDGER BREACH: the exception-ledger row's enumerated C footprint (core + admitted generated parser.c + hand-written scanner.c per grammar) crosses a governance cap — proposed: > N admitted grammars carrying hand-written external scanners (starting N to be set in the W2 IP), OR any required-for-GATE grammar whose scanner cannot be sandboxed (WASM) — at which point the open-ended C surface forces the owned runtime per minimal-deps doctrine.

GRAMMAR-ABI / VERSION-DRIFT INSTABILITY: gate findings or content-hash stability break across a pinned-grammar bump more than a tolerated rate (the nvim-treesitter/difftastic/Helix-documented ABI-skew failure class), measured by the grammar-fleet conformance ratchet — proposed: any GATE-tier finding-code whose anchors shift on a grammar version bump within the same ABI number.

ERROR-RECOVERY-SHAPE NON-DETERMINISM: tree-sitter's undocumented cost-based recovery changes tree shape around in-progress agent edits across a core release such that AUTO-tier fix anchors or affected-set computation become unsound (matklad's incomplete-large-construct case: agent-authored half-written functions attach to ERROR nodes) beyond the tolerance contract.

DESTINATION READINESS (the positive trigger): the owned rowan-style runtime reaches parity on a frozen corpus — proposed gate: byte-identical owned-tree reconstruction + content-hash stability + incremental-reparse latency <= tree-sitter on the W2 benchmark set, per-language parity gates (ADR-0482/0520 bridge-discipline) — at which point the WorkAreaTree impl swaps with no trait change.

GOVERNANCE TRIPWIRE: any move to HARDEN the transitional tree-sitter adapter into the destination (the common fate of 'temporary' parsers) — e.g. trait surface starts leaking TSNode/TSQuery, or the owned identity overlay stops being maintained — immediately violates ADR-0517's one-way door and forces re-evaluation; this is a qualitative trigger but ADR-0517-binding.

phasing: PHASE 0 (LEADS — governance-load-bearing per AMENDMENT 10): Doc-tracking / staleness-gate lane on a CORRECTNESS-GRADE PURE-RUST markdown AST (comrak/cmark-gfm-parity with sourcepos; pulldown-cmark already in third-party/fixups/), NOT tree-sitter-markdown. Land the WorkAreaTree typed cross-file edge model first: file->ADR citation edges + stale_reference / unreachable_doc / broken_link / derived_doc_drift as typed nodes, wired into the gate Finding contract (ADR-0528) with AUTO/ADVISE/GATE tiers (ADR-0519/0529). This lane is pure-Rust (no C, no purity exception) and unblocks AMENDMENT-10 authority chains without waiting for any parser adoption.

PHASE 1 (interface lock, no parser yet): Lock the WorkAreaTree trait shaped for the OWNED destination — content-addressed NodeId, owned node-kind taxonomy, typed edges, incremental edit sessions, owned query handles, Fix-Plan, error-tolerant typed nodes — with the W1 ADR-0520 interface set. Write the ADR recording the ADR-0520 transitional-impl decision + the purity exception-ledger row. NO TSNode/TSQuery in the trait. (WorkAreaTree has no Rust impl yet, so this is destination-first by construction.)

PHASE 2 (transitional adapter, code lane): Implement the tree-sitter WorkAreaTree adapter behind the locked trait for Rust + JSON/TOML/YAML/bash (reindeer/buck2 fixup per grammar crate, mirroring aws-lc-sys; TOML via the maintained tree-sitter-toml-ng fork — flagged weakest link). Build the OYATIE content-address overlay (Merkle hash over the CST, occurrence-disambiguated, re-hash bounded by changed-ranges) — this is the R2 layer and is ours. Curated, pinned, conformance-tested, benchmarked grammar registry (per-grammar parse-rate admission test before GATE-tier; ADVISE-only for unaudited long-tail). Prefer WASM-sandboxed grammar loading for the customer-repo tail.

PHASE 3 (gates + auto-fix on the adapter): AST practice/anti-pattern gates (owned query language over the trait, NOT raw S-expr); behavior-preserving auto-fix as span-anchored Fix-Plans + reparse-verify (tree-sitter has no rewrite API) with the 5 AUTO safety proofs (ADR-0519/0530/0531); work-area affected-set from content-addressed NodeIds; auto-remediation bot fleet (ADR-0531). Windowed gate re-evaluation over changed-ranges (queries are NOT incrementally maintained).

PHASE 4 (destination spike, parallel + non-blocking per ADR-0520): Prototype the owned rowan-style content-addressed runtime — recommended shape is owned safe-Rust incremental-GLR runtime consuming tree-sitter grammar.json tables via the already-Rust tree-sitter-generate crate, with per-language external-scanner Rust ports (bash/YAML the first scanner ports) + handwritten resilient parsers (Biome pattern) for first-party Rust. Stand up the cutover parity harness (byte-identical owned-tree + hash-stability + latency on a frozen corpus). Cutover is event-gated by the numeric triggers, NEVER deadline-gated; swap is a single WorkAreaTree impl with no trait change.
open_questions: Owned-runtime build shape: does Phase-4 consume tree-sitter grammar.json tables via tree-sitter-generate (already Rust) — accepting per-language external-scanner Rust ports as the cost — or author owned grammars (ungrammar-style) for first-party languages and consume tree-sitter tables only for the customer long tail? This is the single biggest schedule/scope lever for the destination and report 4 disagrees with the others on its leverage.

Customer-repo grammar governance (R1 'any repo' vs hermeticity): statically-compiled grammars are a closed set; runtime extension is either Helix-style dylib loading (violates distroless/hermetic posture — REJECT) or wasmtime WASM grammars (adds a heavyweight Rust dep but sandboxes untrusted scanners). Need an explicit ADR on the supported-grammar admission + ADVISE-vs-GATE tiering model for unaudited languages.

Numeric values for the cutover triggers and the exception-ledger C-surface cap (N scanner-bearing grammars) — these are proposed starting thresholds here and must be measured on the production corpus and ratified in the W2 IP (ADR-0510 discipline: measured, re-ratified-not-silently-changed).

Markdown spec-version pinning: comrak tracks cmark-gfm (GitHub dialect); CommonMark and GFM diverge and evolve — the R5 staleness-gate contract must pin a spec version or doc-tracking findings shift under dependency upgrades.

Does the owned content-address overlay's occurrence-disambiguation key (path/parent-chain on top of the content Merkle hash) need to be locked into the W1 WorkAreaTree trait NOW (rowan green-nodes conflate identical subtrees per its own docs; claim-locking and affected-set alias distinct work areas if identity is content-hash-alone)? Recommendation: yes, lock (content_hash, path) as the NodeId in Phase 1.

Query-language ceiling: tree-sitter queries (and any owned syntactic query language) are purely syntactic — practice gates needing name resolution / dataflow (unused import, cross-file dead code) will outgrow them regardless of parser. When does Oyatie need a semantic layer (scope-graph theory per archived github/stack-graphs — adopt concepts not the archived code) on top of WorkAreaTree, and is that a W2 or W3 deliverable?
